title: M_DYN: Indexed lossy store + (addr,old_value) L2 delta (the make_delta the scalar floor lacks)
description: ADR 0009 Decision 2b/4.4. The scalar memory floor (ADR 0014) reverses MemoryStore via L3 ONLY (no make_delta; inverse raises). For a dynamic array, an element write arr[i]=v must push an L2 DeltaEntry capturing (old_value = M[addr],) before overwriting, so unstep! restores the cell; addr is recomputed at inverse time from live SSA operands (base,i,stride). Per-write O(1) delta is mandated over L3 whole-state snapshots (PRD 3.3 forbids full snapshots). Add make_delta + a payload-accepting inverse for the indexed store; this is a NEW layer, not a change to the scalar n_elems=1 store. MUST exercise mixed L2-delta/L3-checkpoint history inside a loop (ADR 0009 Decision 4.7; Rule 2/4). Ref: docs/adr/0009-dynamic-size-memory.md.
notes: CRITICAL SCOPE FINDING (2026-05-31, during Unit 2 recon): ekc is the FIRST L2 delta that needs PRE-state. The push gate (src/interpreter/Interpreter.jl:746) calls make_delta(instr, s_pre, step) but s_pre is bound to s.current AS A SHORTCUT (docstring l.791-808): it is the POST-forward state, safe only because every existing make_delta IGNORES s_pre (empty payload). A MemoryStore (addr,old_value) delta must read the cell BEFORE forward() overwrites it. So ekc REQUIRES a step! change: capture the needed pre-state before forward() and pass it to make_delta — for the L2-marked store only, to preserve L2's space win (a full deepcopy(s.current) per step = L3 cost, defeating the point). Plus the ABSENT-CELL subtlety: memory uses absent=0, but Dict content-equality treats {a=>0} != {}, so the inverse of a store to a previously-absent cell must DELETE the cell, not write 0 (capture was_present; same missing-sentinel issue as ADR 0008 Dict). Design: make MemoryStore L2-capable (make_delta capturing (addr,old_value,was_present) from pre-state + inverse(::MemoryStore,s,::NamedTuple) restoring/deleting), exercise via must_cache_set (compute_must_cache, src/analysis/liveness.jl) in the test, assert history has DeltaEntry not just CheckpointEntry. Scalar floor stays L3 (empty must_cache_set). This is a Core step!-path change — TDD + hostile review.

(Dict content {a=>0}!={}). TDD + mutation-proof (absent-cell per-step test catches what L3 masks; both mutations RED). Hostile review APPROVE-WITH-FIXES (gate semantics preserved exactly, exception-safe, no regression) — fixed the mutation-(ii) comment. Suite 3482/3482. Scalar floor unchanged (empty must_cache->L3). title: M_UNBOUNDED design ADR: collatz ParsedIR->VMProgram lowering convention
description: Keystone design ADR for the collatz vertical slice (user-chosen 2026-05-28: prove the pipeline on collatz_steps end-to-end before generalizing). Decide and document, grounded in RC3 (ADR 0001) + Mogensen RSSA + the existing instruction set: (1) the REVERSIBLE SSA-CREATE convention — how a fresh SSA dest computed from still-live operands (IRBinOp/IRICmp) is lowered reversibly. Candidate: a 'define-then-delete' form (forward inserts dest=f(operands); inverse deletes dest, recompute-on-redo, no history) vs the existing ArithmeticAssignment x:=source⊕(l op r) with a zero-source convention. The existing AA DESTROYS source, so a pure create needs either a new instruction or a zero-init convention. This is the keystone. (2) IRICmp predicates (slt/eq/ugt + LLVM siblings) added to BINARY_OPERATORS/_apply_binop, returning Int64(1)/Int64(0); and the i1->Int64 boolean encoding convention. (3) IRSelect -> reversible 2-to-1 MUX: dedicated SelectInstruction(result,cond,val_true,val_false) reversible as a live-operand create (both branch values stay live in SSA), vs decomposition into existing ops ('MUX-via-CNOT', impl-plan M_OPCODE.2). (4) IRPhi loop-carried merge -> ConditionalEntry params (φ on joins, paired with the back-edge ConditionalExit). (5) IRRet -> EndInstruction. FINDINGS already established: interpreter supports cyclic CFG as-is (no extension); extract_parsed_ir yields the symbolic loop (no reject to intercept). The ADR enumerates the implementation sub-beads (ICmp predicates, SelectInstruction, the ingest, the collatz test M_UNBOUNDED.3 hvx). Per CLAUDE.md Rule 6 (Core: new IR concept/instruction → contested choices get 2-3 independent research subagents before implementing) + Law 1 (cite RC3/Mogensen/Bennett.jl) + Law 2 (reuse RSSA, don't reinvent). Key files: docs/adr/0012-collatz-lowering.md (new); informs src/ir/operators.jl, src/ir/arithmetic_assignment.jl, a new select instruction, and the lower_vm ingest.
close_reason: ADR 0012 (docs/adr/0012-collatz-lowering.md) written, synthesizing the 2+1 design pass. Decisions: D1 dedicated Define instruction (non-injective, L3-reversed) for SSA-creates — rejected widening AA.source because the trace-tape/L3 decision needs prior-value capture, which the '0⊕e then delete' form can't give on overwrite; D2 add COMPARISON_OPERATORS (slt/eq/ugt+siblings) to operators.jl/_apply_binop, nonzero-true i1; D3 new SelectInstruction (MUX, Law-2 exception); D4 IRPhi→ConditionalEntry params, IRBranch→ConditionalExit, IRRet→End, back-edge native; D5 synthetic zero-creates for constant φ-incomings. KEYSTONE FINDING (both proposals missed, orchestrator-caught): loop temporaries are the same SSA names overwritten each iteration → NOT zero-history; user chose trace-tape = existing L3 checkpoint-replay (unstep! restores snapshot + replays forward, never calls per-instruction inverse, so overwrites handled automatically). Pebbling deferred to M9. Risks: i8-vs-Int64 width (R1, use non-overflowing test input + follow-up masking), per-target ConditionalExit args (R2), Define/Select L1/L2 inverse (R3).

title: M11.6: Lean Theorem 3 — RAM-primitive equivalences (Exchange is an Equiv on memory)
description:
Scope: Prove Theorem 3 (RAM-primitive equivalences) in Lean 4: the Exchange instruction is an Equiv on the memory component of IState (i.e., the exchange M[addr] <-> reg is a bijection on the memory-register pair). This closes the PISA memory-access correctness requirement — a load that does not store back is not reversible (cite Vieri 1995 §4.2.1). Prove: exchange composed with itself is the identity. Cite PRD v4 §3.8 Theorem 3 and Kaarsgaard et al. for the Equiv framing.

title: M11.5: Lean Theorem 2 — round-trip (unstep(step s instr) = s for all instruction kinds)
description:
Scope: Prove Theorem 2 (round-trip) in Lean 4: unstep (step s instr) = s holds for every instruction kind defined in Formalisation/Semantics/. This is the load-bearing reversibility invariant. Proof is by case analysis over the instruction ADT. For injective instructions (SwapInstruction, all ControlInstructions) the proof is direct; for non-injective instructions the history payload must be discharged from the delta. Cite PRD v4 §3.8 Theorem 2 and Kaarsgaard et al. join-inverse-categories (round-trip = identity morphism in the inverse category).

title: M11.4: Lean Theorem 1 — trace simulation (abstract step agrees with reference)
description:
Scope: Prove Theorem 1 (trace simulation) in Lean 4: for all prog and all instructions, the abstract step function agrees with the reference irreversible step modulo history projection. Formally: pi_IState(step rstate instr) = ref_step (pi_IState rstate) instr, where pi_IState projects RState to IState. This establishes that adding the history layer does not change the forward computation. Cite PRD v4 §3.8 Theorem 1 and Kaarsgaard et al. join-inverse-categories (the simulation is an inverse-category morphism).

title: M11.3: Lean abstract VM semantics — IState, RState, step, unstep
description:
Scope: Define the abstract VM semantics in Lean 4: IState (program counter, locals, status), RState (IState + history), step : IState -> Instruction -> IState, and unstep : RState -> Instruction -> RState. These are the abstract types over which all five PRD v4 §3.8 theorems are stated. They are the Lean mathematical models of the Julia implementation, not the Julia structs themselves. The Lean types must be structurally isomorphic to the Julia implementation in src/ but defined independently. Cite Mogensen 2016 §3 (RSSA) for IState shape and Kaarsgaard et al. join-inverse-categories for algebraic framing.

LOC estimate: ~200 LOC Lean.

Key files:
- Formalisation/Semantics/IState.lean (new)

- Formalisation/Semantics/Step.lean (new)

title: Static alloca after a dynamic alloca (mixed static/dynamic layout): advance the compile-time cursor past a runtime-sized region
description: Deferred from bennettvm-uil (ADR 0009 Decision 2a multi-array refinement). _lower_alloca! (src/ir/ingest.jl) now ADMITS a dynamic-after-dynamic alloca (the runtime heap_top offset distinguishes them) but STILL fails loud (Rule 1) on a STATIC alloca after a dynamic one: a static alloca uses the COMPILE-TIME bump cursor (next_addr), frozen at the first dynamic region's base, which cannot step past a runtime-sized region — so a static region placed there would ALIAS the dynamic windows. FORCING CONDITION: a static alloca lowered after a dynamic-N alloca in the same routine. FIX: give the compile-time cursor a runtime-aware companion so a static alloca after a dynamic one is placed past the dynamic region (e.g. allocate static regions in a SEPARATE address sub-range from the dynamic-offset range, or fold static allocas into heap_top too). Add a test: a program with [dynamic alloca, static alloca] round-trips with disjoint windows. Until then the fail-loud guard in _lower_alloca!'s static arm stays (the static-after-dynamic error).

title: In-loop / back-edge dynamic alloca (same dest re-executed): remove DynAlloca.forward haskey guard + LIFO heap_top retract
description: Deferred from bennettvm-uil (ADR 0009 Decision 2a multi-array refinement). The runtime heap_top offset now supports >=2 DISTINCT dynamic allocas (distinct dests). But a dynamic alloca RE-executed under the SAME dest (a loop / back-edge reaches it) is still rejected by DynAlloca.forward's haskey(s.locals, dest) guard (src/ir/alloca.jl) — the unconditional-delete L2 inverse would corrupt the prior allocation. FORCING CONDITION: a dynamic-N alloca reached by a back-edge (re-executed). FIX (now tractable with the offset model): remove the forward haskey guard; on re-execution the dest pointer is re-materialised at the CURRENT heap_top (a fresh offset window), and the L2 (base,n) inverse retracts heap_top -= n LIFO. Add a test: a loop body with a per-iteration dynamic alloca round-trips with heap_top restored to 0. NOTE: in-loop allocas are also typically reversed by L3 checkpoint-replay (the loop crux), so the interaction of per-iteration heap_top advance with L3 replay must be verified (the replay re-runs forward, re-advancing heap_top; the checkpoint snapshot must carry heap_top — it does, via deepcopy).

title: ConditionalEntry predecessor labels not validated vs LabelTable — latent landmine for backward-dispatch (M2.15/pebble)
description: Surfaced by l49 hostile review. Hand-built/test VMPrograms (e.g. test_revmap_roundtrip.jl Part B) use sentinel predecessor labels (:nonexistent_b/:nonexistent_d) absent from the LabelTable; the M2.10 ConditionalEntry constructor only requires the two predecessors differ. The runtime never validates predecessor-label existence in forward/inverse/L3-replay, so this is SOUND today (forward-only + L3 replay never dereference predecessor_true/false). A future backward-dispatch pass (M2.15) or pebble-game lowering routing the backward jump via predecessor_true/false from the LabelTable would KeyError. Fix: (a) validate predecessor labels exist at VMProgram construction (fail-loud, Rule 1); or (b) document the forward-only-sentinel pattern in the ConditionalEntry docstring. Non-blocking; latent.

title: DynAlloca inverse O(n) region delete on huge sparse n (perf, not correctness)
description: Surfaced in 0zn hostile review. inverse(::DynAlloca,s,p) does for a in base:base+n-1; delete!(s.memory,a) — O(n) delete! calls. Correct, but a dynamic alloca with n >> written-cells (e.g. a[1_000_000], only a[0] written) does ~n hash-misses on reverse though forward touched few cells. FORCING CONDITION: runtime n greatly exceeds count of cells present in [base,base+n-1]. Fix: delete only keys actually present in the region (collect first to avoid mutate-during-iterate) → O(written). Non-blocking (Rule 9).

title: M6 follow-up: _handle_backward_cross_block_dispatch! for direct-inverse unstep! path
description: The six control-flow inverse() methods (Begin/End at src/ir/control_instructions.jl:231-246, Uncond Entry/Exit at lines 510-523, Cond Entry/Exit at lines 882-895, plus CallInstruction at src/ir/call_instruction.jl:288-291) are pc-only stubs at the per-instruction dispatch layer. They mirror the forward path's split: forward() bumps pc by 1; _handle_cross_block_dispatch! (src/interpreter/Interpreter.jl) handles the cross-block jump. No backward counterpart _handle_backward_cross_block_dispatch! exists. This is fine for M6.3 and M6.4 because Replay.jl uses checkpoint+forward-replay (s.initial fallback handles empty-history boundary cases). It WILL be needed for any future direct-inverse backward dispatch optimization that bypasses the replay path (would currently land at an out-of-block pc on cross-block backward steps). Per-instruction inverses + LabelTable bwd_address lookup are the natural ingredients. Filed at M6.3 close per reviewer assessment (priority P3 — gap is real but the M4.x fallback is sound and this is an optimization not a correctness fix).

title: PRD v4 SC6 anchors at Part IX M5 but RC3 pre-read lives at M0
description:
